observation.visible_scene: A dark concert/stage lighting rig shown in a stereo (side-by-side mirrored) fisheye view. Symmetric trusses carry bright white LED strips and rows of round orange/red dot lights; a diagonal arm of orange dots sits at each top corner. A cluster of smaller outlined fixtures with orange dots sits low-center in each half. Background is pure black.
visible_changes: Over frames 1-31 the orange/red dot lights on the trusses and corner arms gradually brighten and saturate, and the diagonal corner trusses (white outline + orange dots) become progressively more visible, extending from the top corners toward the center, suggesting a slow widening/zoom-out of the view.
The low-center fixture clusters stay in roughly the same screen position throughout, with their dot lights also brightening slightly.
From frame 32 onward, faint volumetric white beams appear emanating from the upper/moving-head fixtures, angling downward and inward.
Frames 33-41 the beams strengthen and cross near the center forming an X pattern, while a crowd of small white human silhouettes at the bottom of the frame becomes increasingly lit and visible.
The left and right halves remain mirror images of the same scene at every step (stereo rendering), not two independent arrangements.
outside_clip_unknowns: What initiates the lighting sequence (the brightening and beam onset are already in progress at the crop start).
The full physical layout of the rig and the actual stage floor / crowd beyond the lit silhouettes.
Whether the beams continue to sweep or hold after the last frame.
uncertain_details: Camera motion is inferred only from structures appearing at the edges; with a black background the zoom-out/field-of-view change is uncertain.
It is unclear whether the low-center outlined clusters are separate hanging fixtures or reflections/ghosts of the upper trusses.
Exact timing of beam onset vs. crowd illumination cannot be separated from the gradual overall brightening.
